I just bought my first kcup coffee machine last month. I don't think coffee myself and my hubby only likes a cup here and there. It never seemed worth making a whole pot of coffee. So I thought this would be the way to go. A quick and easy cup of coffee. Unfortunately, I hadn't planned on it being so easy that he wanted more coffee than normal.  Then the $$$ started adding up quickly on the purchases of kcups.  I was looking at the replacement kcups and was not thrilled with having to remove the holder that pierces the normal kcups and put in the replacement holder. How often would I have to change back and forth between my coffee and the kcup holder. Then I saw the simple cups.  I watched a video on another review and thought why not give it a shot. I am so glad that I did. It was very easy to do. Put the cup in the holder, add the filter, add the coffee , and put on the lid. Putting on the lid is quite easy with the holder/stand.  There you have your own kcups.  I did notice that strength was not quite as strong as the regular kcups. This is not a problem for us. I always have to add more water to the cup after the brewing was done on a regular kcup.  There is a  little water that stays on top of the cup due to the design of the lid. It is very little. I was able to reuse the cup (not the filter).  I just lined up the holes with the piercers in the machine. He is happy to get more coffee. I am happy to be able to use our own coffee.

Received this a a gift.  I prepared the simple cup per directions, placed in the Keurig and began brew. Only about a third of the water went through the cup. Upon inspection I found that the cup filter splits open and the coffee grounds collect in the bottom of the simple cup and clog the drip line. The coffee that did make it to the cup is full of grounds. I tried three time to make a cup of coffee' 1st time filing the filter to 90% capacity, 2nd time to 75% capacity, and the 3rd time filled to 50% capacity. Each brew time I only received about 2 ounces of coffee ground filled coffee. I opened each simple cup and inspected the filters and each one had split in one or more places thus allowing the coffee grounds to clog the machine. Not only did I waste 3 simple cups and filters but also equivalent amount of coffee and 6 teaspoons of sugar. Additionally, I had to dismantle and clean the Keurig receptacle.

I've had these cups, filters and lids before only sold as "Dispose-a-Cup".  I don't know whether they might be different names from the same manufacturer. In any event, I loved them before, but closing the lids without collapsing the cups was a little tricky. These come with an "easy close stand", which is a plastic cylinder. You place a cup in the easy close stand, drop in a filter, fill with the coffee of your choice, then gently but firmly press together until the lid seats and closes. This easy close stand makes all the difference in the world. Being on a really, REALLY tight budget (can you say cheap?), I think it should be 100 sets (not 50) for the price of $14.95, even with Prime shipping. But since I have the Keurig (purchased a few years ago as a Christmas gift for my now late husband) its much better to make cups of the coffee I want.
